### Added
- **The chart brings its own Flux engine** (roadmap#4348, PRD Q1/Q2/Q3/Q9): `helm install` of the meta-package on a cluster without Flux yields a running platform. The new `flux-engine` subchart (`helm/agent-platform/charts/flux-engine`, released with this chart, the only `dependencies:` entry of `Chart.yaml`, `condition: components.flux.enabled`, default `true`) carries the seven Flux CRDs of source-controller and helm-controller and the four Flux Operator CRDs in its `crds/`, and renders the Flux Operator (`ghcr.io/controlplaneio-fluxcd/flux-operator` 0.59.0 as a Renovate-managed pin, web UI off, no network policy — the upstream chart's Deployment/ServiceAccount/cluster-admin binding/metrics Service, lifted verbatim) and one `FluxInstance` named `flux` in the release namespace (`distribution.version: "2.x"` from `ghcr.io/fluxcd`, `components: [source-controller, helm-controller]`, `cluster.multitenant: true` with `tenantDefaultServiceAccount: default`, no network policy). The operator upgrades Flux — controllers, CRDs, stored objects — inside the range on its own. Its values live under `flux-engine:`. `components.flux` is a feature switch, not a component: an entry without a `chart` key takes part in the roster and the enablement logic but renders no release (`templates/components.yaml`). Measured on a fresh kind cluster: `helm install --wait` deployed in about two minutes, the `FluxInstance` Ready at Flux v2.9.5 in 15 s.
- **The tenant identity `agent-platform-flux`**: a ServiceAccount in the release namespace bound to `cluster-admin`, rendered by the subchart; `gitops.serviceAccountName` defaults to it whenever the engine is on, so every platform `HelmRelease` names it (under the lockdown a `HelmRelease` without one runs as the rights-less default account and fails). The fleet keeps `""` and its exempt namespace and renders none.
- **Render guards for the engine** (`agent-platform.validateEngine`): with the engine on, a cluster that already runs Flux — a helm-controller `Deployment` (`app.kubernetes.io/component=helm-controller`) or a `FluxInstance` outside the release namespace, looked up live under the Helm CLI, `--dry-run=server` and helm-controller — fails the render with `this cluster runs Flux; set components.flux.enabled=false or install the chart through it`; `gitops.namespace` set to another namespace fails (the tenant identity lives in the release namespace); with the engine off, turning it off on an installation that runs it fails (an upgrade would delete the operator together with the `FluxInstance` it finalizes and hang). `helm template` sees no cluster and renders the engine.
- **The ordered teardown**: pre-delete hook Jobs (`templates/hooks/`, rendered only with the engine on) — a hook ServiceAccount + ClusterRoleBinding `<release>-hooks` to `cluster-admin` at weight -10, `<release>-teardown-releases` at weight 0 deleting the platform `HelmRelease`s by name in `gitops.namespace` and waiting, `<release>-teardown-engine` at weight 5 deleting the `FluxInstance` and waiting; one plain `kubectl` command each in the distroless `registry.k8s.io/kubectl` (`gitops.hooks.image`, a Renovate-managed pin), restricted pod security, `--ignore-not-found`, `hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded`; weights -6/-5 are reserved for the self-management hooks. `helm uninstall --wait` returns clean in well under a minute; the operator removes Flux including its CRDs (every `HelmRelease` object with them, the agents' included; workloads and Helm storage stay), the four operator CRDs remain, a reinstall is clean. Without the hooks Helm deletes the operator together with the `FluxInstance` and hangs for its timeout (measured).
- **A kind install smoke in the ATS** (`.ats/main.yaml` runs the smoke step with `app-tests-skip-app-deploy: true`; `tests/ats/test_smoke.py`): the Gateway API CRDs, then `helm install --wait` of the candidate with `tests/test-values.yaml` (the kind shape: engine on, muster + dicebear + connectivity, valkey off, muster's OAuth server and the network policies off — the `auto` knobs resolve the rest), asserting the release `deployed`, the `FluxInstance` Ready at a Flux 2.x, every component `HelmRelease` Ready as `agent-platform-flux`, one Helm revision, the operator as field manager of the Flux CRDs; then `helm uninstall --wait` in under a minute with no Flux CRD left and the operator CRDs kept, and a clean reinstall. `execute-chart-tests` runs it on every PR.
- `make verify-engine` (`tests/verify-engine.py`, in CI with Helm 3.17.3): engine off renders no CRD, no hook, no operator, no `FluxInstance`, no identity and no `serviceAccountName`, the fleet shape stays clean; engine on renders exactly the eleven CRDs, the operator objects, the `FluxInstance` (two controllers, multitenant), the identities and the hooks at their weights, every `HelmRelease` names `agent-platform-flux`, the teardown Job names every rendered `HelmRelease`; the two shapes' `OCIRepository`/`HelmRelease` documents are identical but for `serviceAccountName` and the roster; `Chart.yaml`'s only dependency is `flux-engine`, conditional, a local directory, its version and `appVersion` in step with the subchart. `make verify-meta` asserts the pure-renderer rule with the engine off and that the one dependency is not a component pin. README: a quick start (domain, identity, components — nothing about Flux), the engine, clusters that run Flux, uninstalling, Helm versions. **Management clusters need not act**: they carry `components.flux.enabled: false` already (management-cluster-bases#721), and the fleet render with it is byte-identical. Other installations that run their own Flux set the value before upgrading — see UPGRADE.md.
